categories.label: Laptop / Hardware Issue
quick_fixes: Try a full restart — hold the power button for 10 seconds, wait 30 seconds, then turn it back on.
If the screen is black, press Windows + Ctrl + Shift + B to reset the display driver.
If it is slow or frozen, open Task Manager with Ctrl + Shift + Esc and end any process using over 90% CPU or memory.
For headphone or audio issues, right-click the speaker icon in the taskbar, click Open Sound Settings, and make sure the correct output device is selected.
If the laptop is not charging, try unplugging and re-plugging the charger, and check if the charging port has any dust or debris.
For keyboard or mouse issues, try disconnecting and reconnecting the device, or test with a different USB port.

categories.label: Network / VPN Issue
quick_fixes: Toggle your WiFi off and on — click the WiFi icon in the taskbar, turn it off, wait 10 seconds, then turn it back on.
For VPN issues, disconnect from the JPMC VPN, wait 30 seconds, then reconnect. Make sure you are on a stable network first.
Try forgetting the WiFi network and reconnecting — go to Settings, Network, WiFi, Manage Known Networks, forget JPMC-WiFi, then reconnect.
Restart your network adapter — open Device Manager, expand Network Adapters, right-click your WiFi adapter, and select Disable then Enable.
If only certain websites are blocked, it may be a proxy issue — check that your browser proxy settings are set to Automatic.
Run the Windows Network Troubleshooter — right-click the network icon in taskbar and select Troubleshoot Problems.

categories.label: Access / Password Issue
quick_fixes: For a forgotten password, go to the JPMC MyID portal at myid.jpmc.com and click Forgot Password to reset it using your registered mobile number.
If your account is locked after too many failed attempts, wait 15 minutes and try again — accounts auto-unlock after 15 minutes.
For MFA issues, open the Microsoft Authenticator app and check if the time sync is correct — go to app Settings and tap Verify Time.
If you cannot access a specific application, check if your VPN is connected — most internal apps require VPN.
For access to a new tool or system, raise an access request via ServiceNow at servicenow.jpmc.com — your manager needs to approve it.
Clear your browser cache and cookies, then try logging in again — this fixes most SSO login loops.

categories.label: Software / Application Issue
quick_fixes: Close the application completely, wait 10 seconds, and reopen it — this resolves most temporary crashes.
For MS Teams issues, click your profile picture in Teams, go to Settings, and click Clear Cache — then restart Teams.
For Outlook not loading emails, go to File, Account Settings, and click Repair on your email account.
If an application is not opening at all, right-click it and select Run as Administrator.
Check if there is a pending Windows or application update — go to Settings, Windows Update, and install any pending updates, then restart.
For Excel or Word crashes, open the application in Safe Mode by holding Ctrl while clicking the app icon — this disables add-ins that may be causing the crash.

categories.label: Printer / Scanner Issue
quick_fixes: Check if the printer shows as Offline — go to Control Panel, Devices and Printers, right-click your printer, and select See what's printing, then click Printer and uncheck Use Printer Offline.
For a paper jam, turn the printer off, gently remove the jammed paper from the rear tray or front door, then turn it back on.
Clear the print queue — go to Devices and Printers, double-click the printer, and cancel all pending print jobs.
Try removing and re-adding the printer — go to Settings, Bluetooth and Devices, Printers and Scanners, remove the printer, then Add a Device.
Make sure the printer is connected to the same WiFi network as your laptop — check the printer's display panel for its network status.
For scanner issues, ensure the JPMC Scanner Driver is installed — you can download it from the IT Software Portal on the intranet.

categories.label: Other IT Issue
quick_fixes: Try restarting your device — this resolves most common IT issues.
Check the JPMC IT Status Page on the intranet to see if there is a known outage affecting your issue.
Search for your issue on the JPMC ServiceNow knowledge base at servicenow.jpmc.com for self-service solutions.
